title: The current clo-set subscription model needs to be reworked
content:
Currently the system is incredibly fiscally inaccessible based on how the production pipeline is structured or how business is organized. It also begs the question as to how the account admin will bare the $$ of the clients they invite for collaboration. 

Currently the model's price point is $20 per user. In a brand for internal use this is rather reasonable as it works perfectly for collaboration software between your pattern maker, technical designer, creative director etc.

However if you're running a fashion consultation firm or simply want to collaborate a small number of projects with different people it becomes totally nonviable as an option. It also makes it so one person fronts the bill. There's no way for individual users to pay for their own bill.

If I as a contract pattern maker want to make patterns and convey those designs to the clients, I have to pay for each individual client that views their designs. It doesn't make sense. However if I'm a big brand and have multiple styles across multiple seasons but really only need a few collaborators on it makes sense as the bill won't be more than 40-80 dollars. As a contract pattern maker with 5-6 regular clients and their administrators it would cost hundreds of dollars a month with little usage of actual uploads.

I don't need all those workrooms, I just need people to view their designs and tech packs. 

I'd like to pay for this software but currently it doesn't make sense for me to do so as I can have a maximum of 3 users for free so clients can view their designs, then when I have another client I can use another throwaway account, encapsulating each client to their respective account. This account is a throwaway account I used before subscribing with an education discount for clo on another account. 

I just don't think the current sub model is well thought out. It doesn't consider much outside of conventional fashion houses.
